dimensions.note: Reviewed for the new scaleway-key kind. The secret is a bare Scaleway secret key (UUID), marked sensitive by the shared CredentialInputSchema, and reaches only the X-Auth-Token request header -- never the URL, a detail string, or a resource attribute. It is validated against a UUID shape before any request, so an access key id pasted into `secret` is refused rather than sent. `subject` is an IDENTIFIER: parseScalewaySubject accepts only `SCW` + 17 upper-case alphanumerics, which structurally rejects a secret-key UUID, mirroring parsePveSubject ('=') and parseB2Subject (':'). Every detail string interpolates only the validated subject or an HTTP status. String(cause) from a failed fetch carries no headers, so the token cannot leak through it. Confirmed no code path logs the secret.

The probe emits no logs of its own; every outcome travels as a structured ProbeResult, like the other five kinds. Details name the HTTP status or the violated contract (wrong key in body, unparseable expires_at, missing/invalid subject) without echoing response bodies.

Every branch is distinct and tested: fetch rejection -> unreachable; 401 -> authFailed; 403 -> noExpiry (monitoring gap, not an outage -- the same convention github-pat and gitlab-pat already use); 404 -> authFailed (watched key absent, never noExpiry); other non-2xx -> unreachable; non-JSON -> unreachable; a 200 for a DIFFERENT access key -> unreachable; unparseable expires_at -> unreachable; null/empty expires_at -> noExpiry. ADVERSARIAL FINDING, MEASURED: mapping 403 to noExpiry is only safe if Scaleway answers an EXPIRED key with 401 -- if it answered 403, the day the probe key itself expired every entry (including the probe's own) would turn noExpiry, which never notifies, and monitoring would go silent. Measured against the live API rather than assumed: a throwaway key minted with a 3-minute expiry answered 200 before expiry and 401 `denied_authentication` after it; it was then deleted and confirmed gone. So an expired probe key surfaces as authFailed and notifies. The mapping stands.

12 tests added (72 total, all passing): expires_at read and classified at ok/warn/critical/expired; null expires_at -> noExpiry; 401, 403, 404, 5xx each to its status; non-JSON body, wrong-key body and bad timestamp -> unreachable; network failure -> unreachable; missing subject, secret-as-subject and access-key-as-secret all refused with ZERO requests made (asserted by a request counter); exact URL and X-Auth-Token header asserted; trailing slash on scwBaseUrl tolerated; parseScalewaySubject shape rules. Also verified end-to-end against the live API with a read-only probe key: three real keys returned ok with the correct expires_at and day counts, an unknown id returned authFailed, a missing subject returned authFailed, and a send-only key used as the probe returned noExpiry via 403.

Read-only by construction: one GET per entry, no method that can create, rotate or revoke. Re-running is free and side-effect-free. The request carries the shared timeoutMs via AbortSignal.timeout, so a hung endpoint cannot stall the audit.

Scaleway IAM v1alpha1: GET /iam/v1alpha1/api-keys/{access_key} with X-Auth-Token, reading `access_key` and `expires_at` (ISO 8601 or null). The response's access_key is re-checked against the subject. IAM is a global (region-less) API, so https://api.scaleway.com is a correct universal default. Probe-key permissions confirmed live: IAMUserReadOnly + IAMApplicationReadOnly at organization scope suffices to read keys attached to both users and applications, and does NOT grant policy read (GET /policies -> 403), so the probe credential stays narrower than IAMReadOnly. Status-code semantics (401 refused/expired, 403 authenticated-without-permission, 404 absent) measured live, not only stubbed.

No handles, temp files or caches. Response bodies are consumed by .json() where read, and explicitly cancelled (res.body?.cancel()) on every early-return path, so no connection is left holding an unread body.

Adds exactly parseScalewaySubject to the exported surface, matching the parseB2Subject/parsePveSubject precedent so the identifier rule can be asserted directly. probeScalewayKey stays module-private and is reached through probeFor like every other kind. README and example use fictional identifiers only. The archive still publishes only credential_expiry.ts, README.md and LICENSE.md.

scwBaseUrl is z.string().url() with a real default, justified inline (IAM is global). The kind is a new PROBE_KINDS member, so an unknown kind still fails at parse. The `subject` description, previously 'pve-token only' though b2-key already used it, now documents all three kinds and states that scaleway-key REQUIRES it; the requirement is enforced in the probe (authFailed with a clear detail) rather than in the shared schema, because other kinds legitimately omit it.

Not applicable in the usual sense: the probe creates no resources. Recorded behaviour of the watched credential: an expired Scaleway key answers 401 and a deleted one 404; both surface as authFailed, so a lapse cannot read as noExpiry.
Read-only by design. The scaleway-key kind deliberately gains no write path: its probe credential holds organization-wide IAM read, and a write method would turn a monitor into an IAM editor.
Three preflights, all before any network call: secret must be a UUID, subject must be present, subject must match the access-key shape. Asserted by a test that counts requests and requires zero.
Unchanged. Resource instance names still derive from the credential `id`, so a scaleway-key entry maps onto its inventory row exactly as the other kinds do.
Writes the same credential/audit resource shape as every other kind; no new fields, no schema change, so existing queries and notifyToday gating are unaffected.

Model version bumped 2026.09.08.2 -> 2026.09.30.1 with a declared no-op upgradeAttributes, as this model's own comment requires. That entry also covers b2-key, which shipped in 2026.09.09.1 as a new enum member without a model version bump. Purely additive: one enum member and one defaulted globalArg; existing configs parse and behave identically.
